articles.snippet: Rolling coverage of the latest economic and financial news It’s official, UK car sales jumped last month. New car registrations rose by 13.7% to 94,236 units in August, the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders has reported. articles.title: Rijkevorsel kan nu ook 14-jarigen een GAS-boete geven: "Altijd dezelfde groep jonge jongeren die voor problemen zorgt"
articles.snippet: In Rijkevorsel kunnen jongeren voortaan vanaf 14 jaar een GAS-boete krijgen. Tot nu toe was dat pas vanaf 16 jaar. Maar het is altijd dezelfde groep van een 15-tal jongeren, vaak jonger dan 16 jaar, die voor problemen zorgt in de gemeente. De GAS-boete kan oplopen tot 175 euro, maar voordat die wordt opgelegd, zijn er eerst nog bemiddelingsgesprekken en trajecten met de jongere. Ook kunnen er eerst nog werkstraffen worden opgelegd.

articles.title: It’s time for Mark Zuckerberg to resign from Meta | Joan Donovan
articles.snippet: The CEO is the throughline in a history of billion-dollar blunders that have caused real harm, culminating in last week’s settlement Last week, Meta, the parent company of Instagram and Facebook, agreed to a settlement of up to $18bn after dozens of US states accused it of harming children with addictive products. The settlement’s regulatory implications for social media will affect every user, far beyond teens. But if Meta is truly interested in prioritizing the safety of users, the board should request the resignation of Mark Zuckerberg and restructure to put safety above profit. Continue reading...

articles.title: Private equity faces existential crisis in US as unsold companies pile up
articles.snippet: Private equity firms and the companies they own employ over 13 million, from startups to rural hospitals and large retailers, but experts’ concerns of collapse are growing Retail stalwarts Saks and Eddie Bauer filed for bankruptcy. Kmart and JoAnn Fabrics are gone for good, a trail of layoffs and disappointed customers in their wake. Hospital giant Steward Health Care collapsed, costing thousands of jobs and leaving several communities without a local hospital. These once-trusted US companies have one thing in common: they were owned by private equity investors, who load companies with debt when they buy them and squeeze out profits as they restructure. Continue reading...

articles.title: Volkswagen to cut further 50,000 jobs as it ends row with union over revival plan
articles.snippet: Under-pressure carmaker will shed 15% of workforce and halve its product line in sector’s biggest ever restructure The car company Volkswagen has approved controversial plans to shed 100,000 jobs in a battle for survival as it faces fierce competition from Chinese rivals. After the latest round of talks this week, the company announced a further 50,000 job cuts and agreed a staggered end to current production at four German plants: Emden, Zwickau, Hanover and the Audi site in Neckarsulm between 2031 to 2034. There are no specific plans beyond that. Continue reading...
